recipes.hydrationBasis: Water and starter water divided by total flour, including starter flour. Milk/egg/inclusion water is excluded; no effective-water estimate is asserted.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.instructions: Weigh the flour, starter and water. Mix until no dry flour remains. Add the salt and work it through evenly. Cover the bowl.
steps.readinessCue: Confirm the action was actually completed before continuing.

steps.title: Rest and inspect
steps.instructions: Keep the bowl covered. Inspect the dough before handling; this draft timing is a reminder to check, not proof that a rest is complete.
steps.readinessCue: Confirm the action was actually completed before continuing.

steps.title: First fold
steps.instructions: With damp hands, lift one edge and fold it over the centre. Repeat around the bowl without tearing the dough.
steps.readinessCue: Confirm the action was actually completed before continuing.

steps.title: Rest between folds
steps.instructions: Leave covered. If the dough resists stretching, stop rather than force it.
steps.readinessCue: Confirm the action was actually completed before continuing.

steps.title: Second fold
steps.instructions: Repeat a gentle fold. Record the dough temperature or note that it is unknown.
steps.readinessCue: Confirm the action was actually completed before continuing.

steps.title: Observe bulk fermentation
steps.instructions: Keep covered and record a starting mark in a suitable container. Check expansion, bubbles and strength; choose when to proceed based on observations, not the timer alone.
steps.readinessCue: Expansion, aeration and dough strength are observations to record; this draft has no validated percentage-rise threshold.

steps.title: Preshape
steps.instructions: Turn onto the work surface and gather gently into a loose round. Avoid pressing out all the gas.
steps.readinessCue: Confirm the action was actually completed before continuing.

steps.title: Bench rest
steps.instructions: Cover against drying. Check whether the dough has relaxed enough to shape without tearing.
steps.readinessCue: Confirm the action was actually completed before continuing.

steps.title: Shape a boule
steps.instructions: Prepare the chosen basket or tin. Fold and roll the dough to create surface tension without tearing. Place seam-side as appropriate for the container.
steps.readinessCue: Confirm the action was actually completed before continuing.

steps.title: Check the final proof
steps.instructions: Keep covered. Observe expansion and how the dough responds to gentle handling. Use the dough rather than a compulsory countdown to decide whether to bake.
steps.readinessCue: Record expansion and surface condition; no validated numerical readiness threshold is available for this draft.

steps.title: Preheat and prepare equipment
steps.instructions: Arrange the oven and vessel according to their manufacturer instructions. Use suitable gloves, a clear landing area and an oven thermometer if available. Draft set point: 230°C; confirm it for your equipment.
steps.readinessCue: Confirm the action was actually completed before continuing.

steps.title: Load, score and bake
steps.instructions: Transfer carefully to the heated equipment and score if appropriate. Draft starting profile: 20 minutes covered at 230°C, then 20–25 minutes uncovered at 210°C. Confirm doneness for the actual loaf and equipment; do not treat elapsed time as a safety guarantee.
steps.readinessCue: Confirm the action was actually completed before continuing.

steps.title: Cool before slicing

body: Do not taste a culture or dough to test whether it is safe.

guidance.title: Handle raw ingredients and leftovers carefully
body: Keep hands, utensils and work surfaces clean. Separate raw ingredients from cooked food.
Do not taste uncooked dough or batter. Follow appropriate cooking and chilling guidance for the ingredients and your local requirements.
Dairy/egg drafts here have no validated prolonged warm-holding or shelf-life guarantee. Discard age and appearance do not prove safety.
